root_cause.text: The `vc4_save_hang_state()` function had multiple early return paths that directly returned without freeing the `kernel_state` structure that was allocated at the beginning of the function, causing a memory leak when error conditions were encountered.
root_cause.evidence: The patch consolidates two early return statements (at lines 174-176 and 194-196 in the original code) that performed `spin_unlock_irqrestore()` and `return` without calling `kfree(kernel_state)`. The fix introduces a centralized error handling path (`err_free_state:`) that ensures `kfree(kernel_state)` is called before returning, preventing the memory leak when either no jobs are found or kernel_state->bo allocation fails.

This can be parsed with vc4-gpu-tools tools for try
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 214613656b5179f0daab6e0a080814b5100d45f0
Author: Eric Anholt <eric@anholt.net>
Date:   Fri Oct 30 10:09:02 2015 -0700

    drm/vc4: Add an interface for capturing the GPU state after a hang.
    
    This can be parsed with vc4-gpu-tools tools for trying to figure out
    what was going on.
    
    v2: Use __u32-style types.
    
    Signed-off-by: Eric Anholt <eric@anholt.net>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/vc4/vc4_gem.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/vc4/vc4_gem.c
index 5fb0556e001e..39f29e759334 10
bic_trace_step.reason: The `vc4_save_hang_state()` function contains multiple early return paths that directly return without freeing the `kernel_state` structure. Specifically: (1) Line 109: 'if (!kernel_state) return;' - returns without freeing after kcalloc failure, though this is acceptable since allocation failed. (2) Line 115: 'if (!exec) { spin_unlock_irqrestore(&vc4->job_lock, irqflags); return; }' - returns without freeing kernel_state after successful allocation. (3) Line 123: 'if (!kernel_state->bo) { spin_unlock_irqrestore(&vc4->job_lock, irqflags); return; }' - returns without freeing kernel_state after successful allocation when the nested kcalloc fails. These are the critical memory leaks. The function only frees kernel_state in the final else branch (lines 181-183) when vc4->hang_state is already set, but not in the early error paths where kernel_state was allocated but not assigned to vc4->hang_state.

Author: Eric Anholt <eric@anholt.net>

    drm/vc4: Add support for drawing 3D frames.
    
    The user submission is basically a pointer to a command list and a
    pointer to uniforms.  We copy those in to the kernel, validate and
    relocate them, and store the result in a GPU BO which we queue for
    execution.
    
    v2: Drop support for NV shader recs (not necessary for GL), simplify
        vc4_use
bic_trace_step.reason: The provided function is vc4_wait_for_seqno(), not vc4_save_hang_state(). The vulnerability root cause describes a memory leak in vc4_save_hang_state() where early returns skip freeing an allocated kernel_state structure. This function contains no dynamic memory allocation (no kzalloc, kmalloc, etc.) and no kernel_state variable. The function only uses stack-allocated variables (ret, timeout_expire, wait) and performs wait queue operations. Since the vulnerable function vc4_save_hang_state() is not present in this code snippet, has_bug=false. The vulnerability described does not apply to this particular function.
